PLANNING.detail:
Title: Painter's Palette Sorting – Strategy Pattern (Hard)

Intended changes:
- add class `Colour` (record) with fields `String name` and `int hue`, implements `Comparable<Colour>` based on `hue`, overrides `equals` and `hashCode` in both template and solution repositories
- template repository: change `BubbleSort.performSort` signature to `void performSort(List<Colour> input)` and update import statements accordingly
- template repository: change `MergeSort.performSort` signature to `void performSort(List<Colour> input)` and update import statements accordingly
- template repository: rename method `createRandomDatesList` to `createRandomColoursList`, generate random `Colour` objects instead of `Date`, update related helper methods and print statements
- template repository: update TODO comments to refer to colours instead of dates
- solution repository: change `SortStrategy` interface method signature to `void performSort(List<Colour> input)`
- solution repository: update `BubbleSort` implementation to use `List<Colour>` and compare using `Colour.compareTo`
- solution repository: update `MergeSort` implementation to use `List<Colour>` and adjust internal methods to work with `Colour`
- solution repository: modify `Context` class field from `List<Date> dates` to `List<Colour> colours`, rename getters/setters accordingly, update `sort` method to pass `colours`
- solution repository: modify `Policy` class to use `context.getColours().size()` and `context.setColours(...)` and adjust messages to refer to colours
- solution repository: rename variable names in `Client` from dates to colours, update method calls to `createRandomColoursList`, adjust print statements
- solution repository: update helper methods in `Client` to generate random `Colour` objects (random hue and name) instead of dates
- test repository: update all existing test files to import and use `Colour` instead of `Date`, adjust variable names and method calls accordingly
- test repository: update any structure oracle JSON files to expect `List<Colour>` fields and methods (e.g., `Context` field `colours`)
- test repository: add new test `testStability` that verifies sorting algorithms preserve the relative order of equal-colour hue values
- problem statement: rewrite narrative to a creative painter's colour palette theme, keep task markers unchanged
- UML diagram: rename field `dates` to `colours: List<Colour>` in `Context`, update method signatures to use `Colour`, adjust class notes accordingly

Invariants:
- the number of original test cases (identified by IDs) remains unchanged; only an additional test is added
- method and class names that represent the algorithmic pattern (MergeSort, BubbleSort, SortStrategy, Context, Policy) stay the same
- build tooling (Maven) and dependency set stay unchanged
- solution repository must compile and pass all tests
- template repository must compile but fail the graded tests
- the new domain type `Colour` is present in both template and solution and is not part of the structural oracle
- all public method signatures that are graded keep their names, only their parameter generic type changes from Date to Colour consistently across all repositories

Problem statement:
In this exercise, you are a master painter who needs to arrange a palette of colours in a harmonious order before starting a masterpiece. The colours must be sorted according to their hue, and the painter wants to be able to switch the sorting technique on the fly depending on how many colours are on the palette.

### Part 1: Sorting

First, you need to implement two sorting algorithms, in this case `MergeSort` and `BubbleSort`.

**You have the following tasks:**

1. [task][Implement Bubble Sort](<testid>1732</testid>)
Implement the method `performSort(List<Colour>)` in the class `BubbleSort`. Make sure to follow the Bubble Sort algorithm exactly.

2. [task][Implement Merge Sort](<testid>1730</testid>)
Implement the method `performSort(List<Colour>)` in the class `MergeSort`. Make sure to follow the Merge Sort algorithm exactly.

### Part 2: Strategy Pattern

We want the application to apply different algorithms for sorting a `List` of `Colour` objects.
Use the strategy pattern to select the right sorting algorithm at runtime.

**You have the following tasks:**

1. [task][SortStrategy Interface](<testid>1734</testid>,<testid>1738</testid>)
Create a `SortStrategy` interface and adjust the sorting algorithms so that they implement this interface.

2. [task][Context Class](<testid>1733</testid>,<testid>1737</testid>)
Create and implement a `Context` class following the below class diagram.

3. [task][Context Policy](<testid>1736</testid>,<testid>1729</testid>,<testid>1739</testid>)
Create and implement a `Policy` class following the below class diagram with a simple configuration mechanism:

    1. [task][Select MergeSort](<testid>1731</testid>,<testid>1728</testid>)
    Select `MergeSort` when the palette has more than 10 colours.

    2. [task][Select BubbleSort](<testid>1735</testid>,<testid>1727</testid>)
    Select `BubbleSort` when the palette has 10 or fewer colours.

4. Complete the `Client` class which demonstrates switching between two strategies at runtime.

### Part 3: Optional Challenges

(These are not tested)

1. Create a new class `QuickSort` that implements `SortStrategy` and implement the Quick Sort algorithm.

2. Make the method `performSort(List<Colour>)` generic, so that other objects can also be sorted by the same method.
   **Hint:** Have a look at Java Generics and the interface `Comparable`.

3. Think about a useful decision in `Policy` when to use the new `QuickSort` algorithm.
